title: Build router.verify: check every quoted number against claims.json
why: Evaluation rigor. results/NUMBERS.md already claims 'what router.verify checks prose against', but router/verify.py does not exist — the prose-to-claims contract is asserted, not enforced. Success = a module that scans NUMBERS.md, README.md and presentation.html, resolves every numeric literal to a stable claims.json key, and exits non-zero on any orphan.

notes.text:
ACCEPTED. Serves evaluation rigor (criterion 2) and presentation clarity (criterion 3): docs/CONTRACTS.md:54 and ADR-005 both assert "any number quoted anywhere must exist in claims.json under a stable key", and nothing enforces it. Not a rediscovered dead end -- no router/verify.py exists, `entire search` returns only this loop, docs/COST-LEVERS.md has no entry (it covers cost interventions only). No estimator-critic and no leak-hunter dispatched on purpose: the idea makes no quantitative or causal claim and touches neither router/features.py nor any cross-trajectory join.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE IDEA AS WRITTEN -- the implement turn must take both.

(1) Do NOT rebuild the NUMBERS.md half. It is already safe by construction: every numeral in it is interpolated through router/report.py `_Q.__call__` (router/report.py:783-794), which raises KeyError on a key not in claims.json. Measured this turn: 52 prose numerals in results/NUMBERS.md, 0 orphans. Scanning it again buys nothing.

(2) "Resolve every numeric literal to a claims key" is the wrong success test -- it is simultaneously vacuous and over-strict. 28 claims carry small-int values 0..12 (corpus.n_arms=9, model.cv.folds=5, features.block_B.n_columns=4, basis.chars_per_token=4, frontier.hull.n_vertices=3, ...), so README.md's step numbers 1..6 and "Quick start (5 minutes)" all "resolve" by coincidence while carrying no claim at all. Value-matching alone cannot separate a claim numeral from a structural one.

REAL SCOPE = the four git-tracked user-facing artifacts, and it is small. Measured surface with <style> and <script> stripped: README.md 11 numerals, router/console.html 10, templates/presentation.html 0 (still all FILL placeholders -- verifying it BEFORE it is filled tomorrow is exactly the right time), site/index.html 0.

PLAN.
- New module router/verify.py, entry `python -m router.verify`. Reads results/claims.json plus the four artifacts. Exit 0 clean, 1 on orphan, 2 when claims.json is missing (mirror router/gates.py's exit contract).
- Scan text nodes and markdown prose ONLY, never <style> or <script>. Measured justification: the script bodies hold 183 / 278 / 60,405 literals (console.html / site/index.html / site/data.js) of chart geometry and row data, and every single one that "matched" a claim was a coincidental 0/1/2. Scanning them is pure noise.
- LOCALE IS THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS BIT. router/console.html is GERMAN. Line 354 reads "die MDE liegt bei 11,4 pp" -- that is refusal.mde_best_powered_arm_pair.pp = 11.4 written with a German decimal comma, and a naive parser reads it as 114 and reports a false orphan. The parser must accept BOTH the German decimal comma (11,4) and the English thousands comma (10,845), with a stated disambiguation rule.
- Escape hatch for genuinely non-claim numerals (slide numbers "01 -- Frontier", Python "3.10", the year 2026): a NOT_A_CLAIM allowlist, one justification string per entry, size-capped and asserted by a test. Copy the DOCUMENTARY idiom verbatim from tests/test_data_safety.py:271-317 (cap 8, each entry must carry a real justification).
- Do NOT write to site/ -- a hook blocks it. verify only reads and reports there.

SUCCESS MEASUREMENT (all four required).
(a) `.venv/bin/python -m router.verify` exits 0 on the current tree.
(b) It binds router/console.html's "11,4" to refusal.mde_best_powered_arm_pair.pp and its "1000" to corpus.n_trajectories, and prints the binding.
(c) NEGATIVE CONTROL, without which the check is unfalsifiable: perturb one number in a scratch copy of router/console.html, and verify exits non-zero naming file, line and the offending literal.
(d) tests/test_verify.py covers both directions and skips via unittest.SkipTest when results/claims.json is absent -- the tests/test_invariants.py:47-58 idiom -- so `make test` stays green on a clean checkout.

SIZE: one module (~200 lines) plus one test file. Needs no `make all` -- the generated artifacts already exist on disk. Comfortably one 40-minute turn.

IMPLEMENTED on idea/router-verify (83118f2). router/verify.py + tests/test_verify.py + a `make verify` target + ADR-009 + the CONTRACTS.md sentence that now names both enforcers.

ALL FOUR SUCCESS CRITERIA FROM TURN 2 MET, MEASURED.
(a) `.venv/bin/python -m router.verify` exits 0 on the current tree: 41 numerals across 5 artifacts, 0 orphans (README.md 0 after the allowlist, router/console.html 5, presentation.html 36, templates/presentation.html 0, site/index.html 0).
(b) It binds console.html's German "11,4" to refusal.mde_best_powered_arm_pair.pp and its "1000" to corpus.n_trajectories, and prints every binding.
(c) NEGATIVE CONTROL passes in three forms: a perturbed German numeral, a perturbed English one, and the entry point returning 1 -- each naming file, line and literal.
(d) tests/test_verify.py, 11 tests, all skip via unittest.SkipTest when the claims table is absent. make test 93 OK (was 82), make all green, router.gates GREEN 4 pass / 2 warn / 0 fail.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE TURN-2 NOTE ASKED FOR WERE BOTH TAKEN. NUMBERS.md is not rescanned (report.py _Q already raises KeyError). 'Resolve every literal to a key' was not implemented as the test -- the gate reports ORPHANS only, and ADR-009 states why: value matching cannot separate a claim numeral from a structural one.

SCOPE GREW FOR A GOOD REASON. Turn 2 measured presentation.html at 0 numerals because it was still all-FILL; turn 5 built the real deck, so the live surface is 36 prose numerals there, not 0. That is where the module earned its keep.

FOUR REAL BUGS THE FIRST RUN FOUND, all in presentation.html, all now bound rather than orphaned: 3.6%, 41.0% and 92.0% are PERCENT renderings of fraction claims (ope.routed.switched.spend_share, policy.refused.gross_share, recon.cache_read.share), and -3.83 is a SIGNED literal (frontier.gated_router.hull_bound_at_same_spend_pp). A naive parser reports all four as orphans. The percent rule only fires when the numeral is followed by %, or the tolerance would bind anything.

MEASURED LIMIT, RECORDED HONESTLY: perturbing the console MDE from 11,4 to 11,7 is NOT caught, because 11.7 is recon.turns.per_line.claude-fable-5. The negative control uses 11,9 and the comment says why. ADR-009 carries the same limit.

title: Text classifier on the first user message as a routing signal
why: Routing insight. The whole multivariate fit buys only 0.0685 AUPRC over ctx_lines used raw (0.3475 -> 0.4160), which is a thin margin to build a router on. A hand-rolled text classifier over the pre-treatment system+first-user text may carry signal the count features miss. Success = out-of-fold AUPRC above 0.4160 under job-blocked folds, using pre-treatment columns only and excluding the two outcome-derived columns.

notes.text: Already executed by a parallel session on branch text-classifier-finetune (commit 24e7469): ModernBERT fine-tune, frozen-encoder probe, arm-interaction head. Outcome NEGATIVE and adopted nothing — ADR-008 plus docs/POSTMORTEM-textclf.md. corr(Delta_hat, real stratum gap) = +0.042 against a design-based sonnet-opus contrast of +6.8pp stratum-adjusted. title: Close out the single-arm mixture problem — beat it or headline the negative result
why: Evaluation rigor and the off-policy special prize. NUMBERS.md #5: at equal spend the single-arm mixture frontier reaches -3.83 pp while the gated router reaches +0.76 pp, a 4.59 pp gap the wrong way. Either a gating rule closes it, or the honest headline of this project is the negative result, cleanly stated. Success = the frontier figure plots both curves with the gap quantified and a claims key for it.

notes.text: TURN 10 (deck): PARTLY OVERTAKEN BY ADR-014, and its success criterion is now wrong as written. i0003 asks for 'the gap quantified and a claims key for it'. There already IS such a key and quantifying it that way is exactly the defect i0021 closed: both frontier legs are one-sided UPPER bounds, so their difference bounds the true difference in neither direction. The key has been renamed frontier.gated_router.upper_bound_minus_hull_upper_bound_pp precisely so nothing quotes it as a gap. What this idea has already got, on main as ba96b34: the frontier figure plots both curves, the deck and NUMBERS agree on what is bounded and in which direction, and the negative result is headlined honestly -- but reframed. It is no longer 'the routing logic has not earned its complexity'; it is 'tau is too tight for the frontier test to be informative', because the router moves 3.6% of spend against a hull at -3.83 pp and so cannot reach it by arithmetic however well it routes. WHAT IS LEFT, and it is now two separable pieces. (1) A LEGITIMATE gap number, which needs a joint job-clustered bootstrap with both policies evaluated inside the SAME replicate, emitted through router/report.py under its own key -- that is the only construction that yields a two-sided quantity here. (2) The 'beat it' half is now testable in a way it was not before: raise tau until the moved spend share can span the distance to the hull, and see whether the bound still loses. Below roughly 3.8% of spend moved, no rule can win, so any future attempt that leaves tau at 0.170833 is answering the wrong question. An evaluate turn should re-scope this entry to those two before an implement turn takes it.

notes.text: DATA-SAFETY. Not a judgement call, skips evaluate.

Implemented on idea/data-safety-detectors (3bfe5f1). New RepoCarriesNoOpaqueExportToken: extracts every maximal 16-64 character [A-Za-z0-9_-] run mixing letters and digits from all 114 tracked and untracked-not-ignored files, then streams the 101 MB export once and fails on any token the export contains. title: Supervisor budget check interpolates state.json into a python -c source string
why: loop/run.sh:193 builds "import sys;sys.exit(0 if float('$spent') >= ...)" where $spent is the raw printed cost_usd field out of loop/state/state.json. That file is written by every turn's bypassPermissions agent, so a non-numeric value becomes executable Python in the supervisor -- which runs outside any tool-permission boundary and re-evaluates it via stop_reason() at the top of every loop iteration. Found by the turn-4 security review.

notes.text: SECURITY. Fix: pass values as argv, not source text -- "$PY" -c 'import sys;sys.exit(0 if float(sys.argv[1]) >= float(sys.argv[2]) else 1)' "$spent" "$LOOP_BUDGET_USD". Harden state_field, usage_pct, is_rate_limited and the COST extractor the same way as defence in depth. Success = a test that writes a payload string into state.json's cost_usd, runs stop_reason, and asserts the payload did not execute and the loop stopped cleanly.

Fixed on idea/supervisor-untrusted-state (dbd8647). The exploit is real and was measured, not argued: tests/test_supervisor_input.py runs one probe payload down both paths -- through the OLD interpolated form it executes and writes its sentinel, through stop_reason as it now stands the sentinel is absent and the loop stops with 'unreadable cost_usd'. 4 of the file's 9 tests failed before the fix, 9 pass after; make test 91 OK (was 82), make all green, router.gates GREEN 4 pass / 2 warn / 0 fail. Converted all five readers, not just the reachable one: state_field, usage_pct, quota_reset_epoch, is_rate_limited and the per-turn COST extractor. TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE FIXING IT, both now covered. (1) The max-turns guard was switchable off by writing a non-integer turn counter -- [ $turn -ge 40 ] is a shell error on one, and an erroring guard reads as 'do not stop'; new state_int coerces it. (2) The budget check is three-valued now (over / under / unreadable) and fails closed on the third, which is the one a merely corrupt state file reaches by accident. The durable guard is textual: no python -c argument in run.sh may be double-quoted, and none may continue past its closing quote. run.sh also gained a LOOP_RUN_SOURCED guard so the helpers can be sourced without starting a night.

title: The new opaque-token detector cannot catch the incident it was written for
why: tests/test_data_safety.py:512 on idea/integrate-turn7. RepoCarriesNoOpaqueExportToken.OPAQUE_RE requires a token of 16-64 chars, but the three raw identifiers whose removal the class docstring cites (commit af4e78b, docs/POSTMORTEM-textclf.md section 5) are each 11 chars. Measured this turn: all five tokens removed by af4e78b occur in the export (1, 2, 7, 7025 and 9828 occurrences); zero of the five match OPAQUE_RE. The class is green and detects nothing of its stated class. Found by the turn-8 review turn re-running the detector against the diff that motivated it.

notes.text: DATA-SAFETY. Not a judgement call: a green detector that cannot detect its own stated class defeats a control. Fix: lower OPAQUE_RE's floor from 16 to 8 characters and keep the mixed-letters-and-digits requirement. MEASURED COST OF DOING SO, so the implement turn does not have to re-derive it: repo-wide candidate tokens go 27 (floor 16) -> 59 (12) -> 63 (11) -> 73 (10) -> 93 (8). The export scan is one streamed pass over the 101 MB file regardless of set size, so runtime is unchanged at ~3 s; the 16-char floor buys nothing. Expect the lower floor to surface benign candidates (arm ids are already exempted via router.pricing.OBSERVED_ARMS; the tracked session-uuid scratch paths in router/textclf/ are the other likely hit -- see i0020). Success = a test that takes the af4e78b^ version of docs/POSTMORTEM-textclf.md as a fixture, extracts its tokens and asserts the detector flags them, plus make test still green. Do NOT write any of those tokens into a tracked file: read them out of git history at test time, or synthesise same-shape tokens and assert on shape. Keep the masked-output-only rule on failure.

IMPLEMENTED on idea/opaque-token-floor (beb42c2), branched clean from main. MEASURED, not argued: of the five tokens commit af4e78b removed, all five occur in the corpus and the detector matched 0 of them at floor 16; it now matches 5 of 5 (three raw ids via the opaque windows, two placeholder-shaped via the existing shape detector).

THE TURN-8 BRIEF SAID 'lower OPAQUE_RE from 16 to 8'. That was measured and REJECTED, and the note's own cost estimate is where it went wrong. Floor 8 on the single window takes the repo from 27 candidates to 88 -- and 18 of the 88 OCCUR IN THE CORPUS by coincidence (model identifiers, feature-column names, dates). The corpus test would be permanently red for reasons that are not leaks, i.e. muted. The note predicted benign candidates but not that any would collide.

SHIPPED INSTEAD: two windows. Long stays 16-64 over [A-Za-z0-9_-]; new compact window is 8-15 over [A-Za-z0-9] with NO separator, plus two shape rejections. The separator exclusion is the whole trick and it was measured -- every one of the 18 false positives carries a - or a _, and a raw identifier is not hyphenated, so excluding separators below 16 costs no detection and drops false positives 18 -> 1. The last one is a pixel dimension that sits in loop/JOURNAL.md and in the corpus by pure coincidence; rejected by shape. Second rejection is name-plus-size, kept deliberately narrow (single letter/digit boundary only) so an id that alternates stays a candidate -- widening it would discard exactly the shape the compact window exists for. Both are shape rules, not allowlist entries, so neither can grow (same reasoning as ADR-010).

AFTER: 36 candidates over 126 files, 0 corpus hits, runtime unchanged at ~3 s (the scan is one streamed pass regardless of set size).

THE INCIDENT IS NOW A FIXTURE, not a docstring citation. OpaqueDetectorCatchesTheIncidentItWasWrittenFor reads both sides of af4e78b out of history at test time, keeps the removed tokens the corpus knows, and asserts each is caught by one of this file's detectors -- with a separate control asserting the fixture still reproduces (>=3), so the assertion cannot pass vacuously. Watched it fail first, naming three masked shapes. No token is written into any tracked file; failures print masked shapes only, per the turn-8 instruction. CompactOpaqueTokenShapes (9 tests) exercises the pattern rather than the corpus.

ONE TEST PROBE WAS WRONG AND THE RULE WAS RIGHT: L1024tokens is letter-digit-letter, genuinely id-shaped, and the narrow rejection correctly keeps it. Probe replaced and the case kept as its own test so nobody widens the rejection later.

title: The deck's headline +4.59 pp is a difference of two upper bounds, and the comparison it frames is decided by reroute volume
why: presentation.html:65 and :72 on main. Slide 6's largest type is '+4.59 pp - the gap, in the wrong direction'; slide 5 concludes 'the routing logic has not earned its complexity'. Two independent defects, both verified this turn. (1) router/ope.py:594 declares '-> Tuple[None, None, float, dict]' and returns (None, None, hi, diag): non_inferiority_bound yields a ONE-SIDED UPPER bound only, and both frontier legs are built from it. 4.59 = upper(router) - upper(mixture), which bounds the true difference in neither direction, so no directional conclusion follows from it. (2) The identified delta is sum(W * 1[switched] * (m - y)) with m,y in [0,1] and spend weights summing to 1, so |delta| <= the switched spend share = 0.035888 = 3.5888 pp -- while the hull at matched spend is -3.8322 pp. The gated router cannot reach the hull by arithmetic no matter how well it routes; the slide measures that it moves 3.6% of spend, not that its rule is bad. Found by the turn-8 review turn via estimator-critic and confirmed by hand against claims.json and router/ope.py.

notes.text: HIGHEST PRIORITY OF THIS REVIEW and it skips evaluate: this is not a judgement call about emphasis, it is a number presented as a bound that is not one, on the slide that carries the argument. Judging criterion 1 is exactly 'a number that does not trace' and criterion 3 is presentation clarity; a judge who asks 'in which direction does 4.59 bound the gap?' currently gets no defensible answer. FIX, in this order. (a) Stop printing 4.59 as 'the gap'. Either drop it or rename the claims key to what it is -- a difference of two one-sided upper bounds -- and say so in the caption. (b) Say the arithmetic ceiling out loud, because it is the honest and much stronger statement: the router moves 3.6% of spend (ope.routed.switched.spend_share = 0.035888, 119 of 675 routable), which caps its spend-weighted friction delta below the 3.83 pp the hull sits at, so no router at this tau could pass this test. That reframes the negative result from 'our rule is bad' to 'we chose tau too conservatively to have earned a frontier comparison', which is both true and more defensible. (c) The closing line 'At equal spend, one cheap arm beats our router' is wrong twice: the comparator at that spend is a RANDOMISATION, not a single arm, and ~40% of its weight sits on claude-opus-5, the most expensive arm on the chart. Restate it. (d) If a real gap number is wanted, it must come from a joint job-clustered bootstrap with both policies evaluated inside the same replicate, added through router/report.py under its own key -- do NOT paste a number an agent computed in scratch. Success = presentation.html quotes no quantity that is a difference of two one-sided bounds, router.verify still exits 0, and NUMBERS.md and the deck agree on what is bounded and in which direction. DO NOT use the '4.59 < 11.4 MDE' argument: refusal.mde_best_powered_arm_pair.pp is an unweighted arm-pair rate contrast, a different estimand, and asserting it would be an own goal.

FIXED AND ON MAIN as ba96b34, by the turn-10 deck turn, at source rather than on the slide. All four parts of the turn-8 brief taken. (a) The claims key is renamed to frontier.gated_router.upper_bound_minus_hull_upper_bound_pp -- value unchanged, but no prose can now quote it as 'the gap' without the key name contradicting the sentence. Only two call sites existed, both in router/report.py. (b) The arithmetic ceiling is stated in NUMBERS #5, on the chart and on slide 5: the identified delta is a spend-weighted mean of per-run differences in [0,1] over switched runs only, so it cannot exceed the 3.6% of spend the router moves, and no policy at this tau reaches a hull at -3.83 pp. policy_point now carries switched_spend_share on EVERY plotted point and it is a new frontier CSV column, so the ceiling is a property of each point rather than a sentence about one. CROSS-CHECK WORTH KNOWING: computed on the figs path it is 0.035888244943512816, equal to ope.routed.switched.spend_share computed on the independent OPE path -- two code paths, same digits. (c) The close slide's comparator line is corrected: at $375.45 the hull is an interpolation between claude-sonnet-5 ($172.47) and claude-opus-5 ($686.55), i.e. a randomisation with roughly 40% of its weight on the most expensive policy on the chart, not one cheap arm. title: The per-ref data-safety scan fails open: any git error becomes 'branch clean'
why: tests/test_data_safety.py:267 plus loop/push_gate.sh:59 on idea/integrate-turn7. _repo_files() returns None on OSError or CalledProcessError; every content test then raises unittest.SkipTest instead of failing, and python -m unittest exits 0 when everything skips. ds_scan_ref reads only that exit code, so the branch is reported clean having enumerated zero files, and push_all_branches pushes it. PROVEN this turn without any exotic input: DATA_SAFETY_SCAN_REF=refs/heads/no-such-branch-xyz python -m unittest tests.test_data_safety exits 0 with 'OK (skipped=6)'. Same fail-open shape in RepoCarriesNoOpaqueExportToken, which skips outright when export/ is absent or partial -- so on a machine without the export the headline raw-id detector is inert and green. This is the i0010 fail-open class reappearing inside the gate written to close it. Found by the turn-8 review turn (security-reviewer and the code-review skill converged on it independently).

notes.text: DATA-SAFETY. Fix: treat any git-subprocess failure during a scan as RED, never skip. Concretely -- (1) _repo_files() must raise rather than return None when SCAN_REF is set, since 'git is unavailable' is a plausible excuse on a developer laptop and never a plausible one for a ref the gate just enumerated from for-each-ref; (2) ds_scan_ref must not trust the exit code alone -- have the suite print a machine-readable line naming how many files it actually enumerated and how many tests it ran, and have push_gate.sh refuse the branch when that count is zero or the line is absent; (3) RepoCarriesNoOpaqueExportToken must FAIL, not skip, when export/ is missing while the gate is running, since an inert detector is indistinguishable from a clean repo. Success = a test that points DATA_SAFETY_SCAN_REF at an unresolvable ref and asserts a NON-zero exit, plus a test that stubs the export away and asserts the opaque-token class fails rather than skips, plus the existing 140 stay green. Related but separate: ds_scan_ref re-runs the whole module per branch, redoing the 101 MB export walk ~11x per turn; scope it to the classes that need it while you are in here.

IMPLEMENTED on idea/scan-fails-closed (c3cf051). ADR-015. All three parts of the turn-8 brief taken, plus the efficiency note.

REPRO FIRST, on main, exactly as the finding stated: DATA_SAFETY_SCAN_REF=refs/heads/no-such-branch-xyz python -m unittest tests.test_data_safety exits 0 with 'OK (skipped=6)'. Against the pre-fix code the 10 new cases go 9 red / 1 green, and the one that passes is the control asserting a missing export still only SKIPS outside the gate -- i.e. the suite is not simply stricter everywhere.

(1) STRICT, implied by SCAN_REF and settable as DATA_SAFETY_STRICT=1. _repo_files raises ScanCannotRun on a git error AND on an empty listing -- the second matters, a ref resolving to an empty tree is the same fail-open by another route. New _require_export raises when the export is absent or empty, so the raw-id detector can no longer be inert and green. Outside the gate both stay skips, which is what keeps make test green on a machine without the 101 MB export; that distinction is tested in both directions.

(2) The gate stopped trusting the exit code. The suite prints DATA-SAFETY-RECEIPT ref= files= ran= skipped= failed= from a gate runner in __main__, and ds_receipt_ok refuses on absent line / files=0 / ran=0 / failed!=0. push_gate.sh therefore invokes 'python -m tests.test_data_safety', not '-m unittest' -- only the former prints a receipt, so the old invocation cannot silently satisfy the gate.

(3) Scoped per the note: under SCAN_REF only the four REF_AWARE classes run. HONEST SIZE OF THAT WIN -- 21 tests / 5.0 s -> 16 / 4.6 s per ref, not the big saving the note hoped for, because the opaque detector's own streamed export pass dominates and is genuinely per-ref (candidate tokens differ per branch).

MEASURED ON THE REAL GATE, not only in the harness: ds_scan_ref against this repo's twelve real branches now returns a concrete enumerated count each (83..126, all GREEN), and refs/heads/zz-nope is RED with files=0 ran=7 failed=3.

The existing stub scanner had to learn to print a receipt, which is the contract made visible.

title: Branch names reach git push and the ref scanners as bare arguments, so an option-shaped ref name executes code
why: loop/push_gate.sh:91 and :101 on idea/integrate-turn7 ('git -C ROOT rev-parse $br', 'git -C ROOT push -q $REMOTE $br'), plus tests/test_data_safety.py:259 ('git ls-tree -r --name-only -z $SCAN_REF') and :108 ('git cat-file $ref:$rel'). None uses a -- separator. git branch and git checkout -b refuse option-shaped names, but git update-ref and a direct write under .git/refs/heads do not, and a turn agent runs with bypassPermissions and unrestricted bash. The turn-8 security reviewer built a throwaway repo with a ref named as a --receive-pack= assignment and ran this branch's own push_all_branches against it: git push spawned the named program, which executed locally as the operator's user, while the gate logged only 'WARN: push of ... failed'. The same name makes ls-tree exit 129, which lands in the fail-open path of i0022, so such a branch is reported clean AND then triggers the push. Reachable from every supervisor turn (loop/run.sh:342) and from loop/bootstrap.sh:112 with PUSH=1 shipped as the default.

notes.text: SECURITY. Fix in two layers, both cheap. (1) Validate before use: run 'git check-ref-format --branch $br' on every name coming out of for-each-ref and refuse the branch loudly if it does not pass -- an option-shaped ref in this repo is never legitimate and should stop the push cycle for that branch, not be silently pushed. (2) Add the -- separator everywhere an attacker-influenced name is an argument: 'git push -q $REMOTE -- $br', 'git rev-parse -- $br', 'git ls-tree -r --name-only -z $SCAN_REF --', and pin the push to the SHA that was scanned rather than re-resolving the name ('sha=$(git rev-parse --verify $br^{commit})' once, then push $sha:refs/heads/$br) which also closes the scan-then-push TOCTOU the reviewer raised. Success = tests/test_push_gate.py grows cases whose branch names lead with a dash, carry an = option shape, contain a space and contain a glob character, asserting each is refused and that the clean branches in the same cycle still push. The existing suite only exercises ordinary identifiers, which is why it is green despite this.

SCOPE CORRECTION, verified after filing: this is NOT introduced by idea/integrate-turn7. main already carries the identical bare-argument form at loop/run.sh:182 and loop/bootstrap.sh:100 ('git push -q $REMOTE $br'). The branch moves it into push_gate.sh unchanged. So it is pre-existing debt, the branch is not a regression on this axis, and this finding must NOT block the merge -- fix it in its own implement turn, in push_gate.sh once the branch has landed so it is fixed in one place rather than three.

IMPLEMENTED on idea/ref-name-injection (d83aa59). The exploit is real and was MEASURED, not argued, in a throwaway repo on git 2.55 before anything was changed: git update-ref accepts refs/heads/--receive-pack=<prog>, for-each-ref lists it, git rev-parse echoes it back with exit 0 (so the gate's || continue did not catch it), and git push -q origin '--receive-pack=<prog>' spawns that program locally as the operator's user -- the payload ran and left its sentinel. In the gate's exact single-argument call it looks harmless ONLY when the checked-out branch has no upstream; with an upstream configured, as main has here, it fires. The same name makes git ls-tree exit 129, which is the i0022 fail-open path.

BOTH LAYERS FROM THE TURN-8 BRIEF TAKEN. (1) ds_ref_name_ok validates every name from for-each-ref before it becomes a git argument -- an ALLOWLIST ([A-Za-z0-9._/-], no leading dash) with git check-ref-format behind it as a second gate, because check-ref-format is not sufficient: it returns 0 for refs/heads/--receive-pack=x, measured. A failing name stops that branch loudly and marks the cycle refused; the clean branches still push. (2) The branch is resolved ONCE with --end-of-options to a commit and everything downstream uses the sha: the scan is DATA_SAFETY_SCAN_REF=<sha> and the push is 'git push -- <sha>:refs/heads/<name>'. That closes the option shape and the scan-then-push TOCTOU the reviewer raised in the same move. tests/test_data_safety.py refuses an option-shaped or whitespace-carrying SCAN_REF at import rather than scanning nothing, and its git calls carry separators.

ONE MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF. It asked for four hostile shapes end to end. Two are unreachable: git update-ref REFUSES a name with a space or a glob character, and for-each-ref warns and ignores a ref file written by hand. They are exercised against the validator directly instead, and the note says so rather than claiming an end-to-end test that cannot exist.

ONE NON-OBVIOUS FINDING: git ls-tree does NOT accept --end-of-options before the tree-ish -- it silently returns NOTHING, which is exactly the failure being defended against. The separator goes after the tree-ish, where a pathspec would. cat-file and rev-parse both accept it.

EVIDENCE. tests/test_push_gate.py::BranchNamesAreValidatedBeforeTheyReachGit (7) and ::ScanRefIsNotHandedToGitAsAnOption (3), watched to fail first. The refusal test is paired with a POSITIVE CONTROL that the payload does fire when the name is a bare argument, without which it would prove only that the throwaway repo was broken; and the validator has a negative control pinning the six names this repo actually uses, so a validator that refuses everything -- and so silently stops backing the night up -- cannot pass. Mutation-tested: neutering the character class fails 8 of 21, pushing by name instead of the scanned sha fails 1. GATE: make test 150 OK (main is 140), make all green (301 claims), router.gates GREEN 4 pass / 2 warn / 0 fail, router.verify PASS on 44 numerals across 5 artifacts, tests.test_data_safety 21 OK on the working tree and under SCAN_REF=HEAD. No claims key touched, so no number-verifier. ADR-017.

MERGE NOTE: this branch touches loop/push_gate.sh and tests/test_data_safety.py, and so does idea/scan-fails-closed (i0022/i0024/i0026). Expect conflicts in ds_scan_ref and around the SCAN_REF constant. The two fixes are complementary -- i0022 makes a check that cannot run RED, this one stops the name from breaking the check in the first place -- so take BOTH sides, do not pick one. i0024's move of the __main__ guard in tests/test_push_gate.py will also conflict at the file tail; this branch appended two classes after it.

title: router.verify's prose stripper leaks numerals from an unclosed markdown fence and from a > inside a quoted attribute
why:
router/verify.py:161 and :160 on idea/integrate-turn7. (1) _FENCE_RE requires a CLOSING fence, and unlike the HTML path there is no open-fence-at-EOF fallback -- verify.prose('... ```bash run-command --threshold 999 ','markdown') leaves 999 in the scanned prose, so a dropped closing fence in README.md either fails the gate for the wrong reason or mis-binds a shell literal to a small-int claim. only 7 remains
','html') leaks the 2 that no reader ever sees. (3) The percent lookahead at :260 slices a fixed 2 characters, so two spaces before a % silently disables the claim-as-fraction path and a legitimate percent reports as an orphan. If the evaluate turn accepts, success = tests/test_verify.py gains an unclosed-fence markdown case and a >-inside-attribute HTML case, and the percent lookahead scans to the next non-space rather than slicing 2 characters.

notes.text:
All four branches merged onto idea/integrate-turn12, in ADR order: idea/scan-fails-closed (i0022+i0024+i0026, ADR-015), idea/opaque-token-floor (i0018, ADR-016), idea/ref-name-injection (i0023, ADR-017), idea/verify-missing-artifact (i0019, ADR-018). TWO REAL DEFECTS THE INTEGRATION FOUND, neither visible to any branch alone; both fixed test-first, watched red then green.

(1) 7db12be. i0018 added OpaqueDetectorCatchesTheIncidentItWasWrittenFor with a bare os.path.isdir(EXPORT) skip guard. i0022 had meanwhile made 'the export directory exists but is EMPTY' a first-class case and routed every other export-backed check through _require_export, which knows that state is a skip outside the gate and RED under STRICT. isdir says yes to an empty directory, the export scan then answers 'the corpus knows none of these tokens', and the control reads that as its fixture commit having stopped reproducing the incident -- so it FAILED where it must skip. (2) c78eb40. i0022 made a green exit code insufficient: a scan counts as clean only when it prints a receipt naming how many files it enumerated and how many tests ran. i0023's end-to-end tests drive push_all_branches against a throwaway repo with stub scanners standing in for that suite, and those stubs only exit 0. Both stubs now speak the receipt protocol via a shared RECEIPT_LINE constant that says why.
